questions.q: What four things does a clean escalation hand off to Tier 2?
options: The analyst's contact information, a screenshot, and nothing else
Only the original alert text, unmodified
A guess about severity and a request to "take a look"
The classification already reached, the scope already established, the evidence already gathered, and a clear reason for escalating
questions.explain: Those four pieces let Tier 2 start exactly where Tier 1 left off instead of re-running work that's already been done.

questions.q: Why does a messy escalation like "this looks bad, escalating" with no case note end up costing more time overall?
options: Ticketing systems reject escalations that lack a case note
It costs nothing extra -- Tier 2 always re-validates every alert regardless of what Tier 1 provides
Tier 2 is required to send it back to Tier 1 unopened
Tier 2 has to re-validate the alert from scratch, which is slower than if Tier 1 had simply finished the validation themselves
questions.explain: Skipping the handoff pieces doesn't eliminate the missing work -- it just moves it downstream onto a team with less availability.

questions.q: What is a ticketing system's role in escalation, according to this lesson?
options: It's only used for alerts that turn out to be false positives
It's the default path -- the case note and evidence get attached to a ticket and routed to the Tier 2 queue
It replaces the need for a case note entirely
It is used only during quarterly audits, not day-to-day escalation
questions.explain: The ticketing system is the default escalation channel, carrying the case note and evidence to Tier 2's queue.

questions.q: When does a direct handoff -- a call, page, or incident-channel message -- get used alongside the ticket?
options: Never -- tickets are always the sole escalation channel
When something can't wait for the normal queue, such as active data exfiltration in progress
Only when the ticketing system is offline
For every single escalation, regardless of urgency
questions.explain: A direct handoff supplements the ticket for urgent cases, getting a human on the case immediately while the ticket still records it.

questions.q: What decides whether an escalation gets an immediate page in addition to a ticket?
options: The alphabetical order of the affected account's username
Severity has no effect on how an escalation is routed
Whichever analyst happens to be on shift at the time
Severity-based routing -- a confirmed critical case triggers an immediate page or call on top of filing a ticket
questions.explain: Most SOCs route by severity: a critical incident gets an immediate page alongside the ticket, while a less urgent high-severity case rides the normal queue.
